MCD.rationale: McDonald's franchise quality is exceptional — 95% franchised, ~46% operating margins, ~210M loyalty users, and a Q1 2026 earnings beat (adj. EPS $2.83 vs $2.75 consensus, revenue $6.52B vs $6.46B expected). YoY fundamentals are solid: revenue +9.4%, EPS +6.9%, global comps +3.8%. The balance sheet carries structural negative equity ($-1.29B) with ~$61B liabilities, but OCF/NI of 1.22x confirms cash quality and the equity position is improving sequentially. However, the macro backdrop is genuinely challenging — WTI at $98.38, 10Y at 4.41%, Baa spreads at 6.06% — and management itself flagged consumer softness heading into Q2. The stock is at its 52-week low ($283.70, near $282.15), which may reflect these headwinds rather than fundamental deterioration. Valuation cannot be precisely confirmed due to non-functional ratio data, but the rough P/E is likely in the low-to-mid 20s (the quant estimate of ~24.3x is overstated due to missing Q4 2025, which would be seasonally strong). The Q1 beat and 2026 guidance (mid-to-high-40% margins, ~2,600 openings, 50K units by 2027) provide a modest near-term positive signal, but consumer headwinds and elevated oil/rates cap the upside. Net: a high-quality franchise at a reasonable but not clearly cheap price, with real macro headwinds and a negative turn in recent news sentiment (two -1.0 readings). Mildly attractive.
key_factors: Q1 2026 earnings beat: adj. EPS $2.83 vs $2.75 consensus, revenue $6.52B vs $6.46B expected; global comps +3.8% across all segments
YoY growth intact: revenue +9.4%, EPS +6.9%, gross profit +9.5% vs Q1 2025
Franchise model produces ~46% operating margins (FY2025), ~89.6% gross margin, 95% franchised with 20-year agreements
Loyalty ecosystem: ~210M 90-day active users, ~$40B systemwide loyalty sales, members visit 2.5x more often
2026 guidance: mid-to-high-40% operating margins, ~2,600 openings, targeting 50,000 units by 2027
Balance sheet: negative equity -$1.29B with ~$61B liabilities; OCF/NI 1.22x confirms cash quality; equity improving from -$2.16B in Q3 2025
Macro headwinds: WTI $98.38 (+52% over lookback), 10Y yield 4.41%, Baa spread 6.06% — rising costs and discount rates
Consumer softness: CEO warned spending 'getting a little bit worse'; Q2 faces tough comps from prior-year Minecraft tie-in
Stock at 52-week low $283.70 (touched $282.15 on 2026-05-07), -12.3% quarterly drawdown
Recent news sentiment turned negative: two -1.0 readings on 2026-05-04 and 2026-05-06
Dividend: $1.86/share quarterly, 49-year consecutive growth streak, ~2.5% yield
Valuation unconfirmed: supplied P/E ratios non-functional; rough estimate ~24.3x but unreliable due to missing Q4 2025 data

sources_cited.excerpt: Adjusted earnings per share of $2.83 beat Wall Street's forecasts for $2.75. Revenue grew 9% year over year to $6.52 billion, slightly above the $6.46 billion the Street expected.
Global Systemwide sales increased 11% (6% in constant currencies) to over $34 billion for the quarter... Diluted earnings per share was $2.78, an increase of 7%.
For 2026, the company targets roughly 2.5% Systemwide sales growth from net unit expansion, mid-to-high-40% operating margins, and low-to-mid 80% free cash flow conversion.

The MyMcDonald's Rewards loyalty program reached ~210 million 90-day active users by year-end 2025, up 19% YoY, generating ~$40 billion in systemwide loyalty sales (target: $45 billion by 2027 and 250 million users).

McDonald's CEO says consumer spending could be 'getting a little bit worse'... CFO Ian Borden said McDonald's was already anticipating a deceleration from the first quarter, even before consumer sentiment weakened.
Rising oil prices ($4.20/gallon) and geopolitical tensions in Iran are dampening consumer spending, forcing fast-food chains to intensify value promotions.
